facts.program: Efficiency Manitoba air source heat pump rebate
facts.claim: $2,000 rebate for a centrally ducted cold climate air source heat pump or $1,500 for a ductless cold climate air source heat pump. The contractor submits the application within 90 days of installation and a cheque is mailed; a post-verification inspection may be required. Rebate for a cold climate air source heat pump. The retrofit must supplement an electric resistance or natural gas heating system; homeowners converting from propane or fuel oil are also eligible. Your contractor submits the application within 90 days of installation and a rebate cheque is mailed. A post-verification inspection may be required.
facts.amount: $2,000 ducted or $1,500 ductless $2,000 for a centrally ducted cold climate air source heat pump. $1,500 for a ductless cold climate air source heat pump.
facts.eligibility: Residential property, existing home (new homes are not eligible). Primary (not seasonal) residence. The contractor must be registered with Efficiency Manitoba. The retrofit cannot replace an existing heat pump system. Apply for Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan before any work starts if you want financing. Earlier note: Retrofit that supplements an electric resistance or natural gas heating system (homeowners converting from propane or fuel oil are also eligible); residential property, new homes not eligible; contractor registered with Efficiency Manitoba; primary (not seasonal) residence; not replacing an existing heat pump system.
facts.dates: No closing date stated. A $100 supplier bonus runs to March 31, 2027 (paid to suppliers, not homeowners).
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. Read 2026-10-10. Terms and conditions and program guide PDFs were not opened. Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan can be added; apply for financing before any work starts.

facts.program: Efficiency Manitoba ground source heat pump program
facts.claim: Qualifying homeowners can install a ground source heat pump with no upfront cost and an interest-free monthly payment of $75 for 15 years (total $13,500). Retrofit projects over $38,000 and replacement projects over $18,500 need an upfront contribution. The loan becomes due when the house is sold or ownership transfers and is not transferable.
facts.amount: $75 a month for 15 years, interest free ($13,500 total)
facts.eligibility: Retrofit replacing an electric furnace or boiler, electric baseboards or natural gas heating (fuel oil conversions also eligible); new homes eligible; registered contractor who is a member of the Manitoba Geothermal Energy Alliance; primary residence. Wait for written approval before work; one year to install.
facts.notes: Read 2026-10-10. Enhanced offer under the Affordable Home Energy Program.

facts.program: Efficiency Manitoba Energy Efficiency Assistance Program
facts.claim: Free air source or ground source heat pump when retrofitting a qualifying home that now has an electric furnace, baseboard heaters or an electric boiler. Also free energy assessment, insulation and a smart thermostat, and a $5,000 rebate for a high-efficiency natural gas boiler. Free and subsidized energy efficiency upgrades for income-qualifying households. The program finds the upgrades, connects you with registered contractors and handles the upfront payment. Open to income-qualifying homeowners, renters, landlords, and First Nation people living off-reserve or owning a home on reserve.
facts.amount: Free heat pump (electric-heated homes) Free or subsidized upgrades (no dollar amount stated).
facts.eligibility: Single-detached or semi-detached home, lived in year-round. Total household income before deductions at or below: 1 person $46,264; 2 people $57,595; 3 people $70,806; 4 people $85,968; 5 people $97,504; 6 people $109,967; 7 or more people $122,432. Earlier note: Single-detached or semi-detached home lived in year-round; household income at or below $46,264 (1 person), $57,595 (2), $70,806 (3), $85,968 (4), $97,504 (5), $109,967 (6) or $122,432 (7 or more), or a First Nation band member with status; income verification for all residents 18 and older; property value and assets may also be reviewed. Owners, renters and landlords can apply.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. An initiative of the Affordable Home Energy Program. Read 2026-10-10. Red River Métis Citizens have a separate offer (efficiencymb.ca/my-home/metis-energy-offers/), not read in full.

facts.program: Manitoba Hydro Home Energy Efficiency Loan
facts.claim: Efficiency Manitoba says qualifying upgrades, including heat pumps, can be financed with Manitoba Hydro's Home Energy Efficiency Loan, with a chosen term and payments added to the energy bill. Apply for financing before starting any work, including buying products.
facts.notes: Loan limits and the interest rate were NOT confirmed: Manitoba Hydro's pages and supplier guides disagree on the per-home cap and no official rate was found. Do not state them.

facts.program: Federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (Manitoba)
facts.claim: July 31, 2026 was the last day to apply. Applications sent before then are still processed; final receipts and the attestation form are due January 31, 2027.
facts.eligibility: Closed. Applied to oil-heated homes at or below median household after-tax income.
facts.notes: The page lists Manitoba among the covered provinces; read 2026-10-10.

facts.claim: Rebates for insulation upgrades to attics, walls and foundation walls, plus an air sealing bonus. Get approval before buying materials or starting any work, including removing drywall, stucco or old insulation. You have 12 months from approval to install. The air sealing bonus needs a pre-retrofit and post-retrofit EnerGuide evaluation and comprehensive air sealing done before the insulation.
facts.amount: Per square foot, by R-value added: attic (open) from R-34 or less to R-50 to R-60: $0.03 per R per sq ft. Cathedral, sloped or flat roof from R-30 or less to R-28 to R-60: $0.03. Attic kneewall from R-12 or less to R-24: $0.03. Wall cavities from R-12 or less to R-12 to R-24: $0.06. Exterior wall when re-siding from R-0 to R-3.75 to R-15: $0.15. Foundation walls and joist headers from R-12 or less to R-22 to R-24: $0.06. Air sealing bonus: up to $1,000.
facts.eligibility: You own the residence (home, rental property or cottage). The residence has active Manitoba Hydro residential service. Free insulation may be available through the income-based and Indigenous offers.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. The page text on heating-fuel conditions was cut off, so none are stated.

facts.claim: Rebate on each ENERGY STAR certified window, entry door and sliding glass door with at least triple pane glass (entry doors with no glass must be ENERGY STAR certified). Apply within 90 days of installation and full payment. An NRCan reference number is needed for each window and door.
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR certified with at least triple pane glass.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. A total cap per home was not on the page.

facts.claim: $50 rebate on an ENERGY STAR certified smart thermostat. A new ecobee for electric heating and cooling may also earn Peak Partners money: $50 for enrolling plus $25 for each Peak Partners season, up to $150 in rebates and incentives in the first year.
facts.amount: $50 (up to $150 in the first year with Peak Partners and an eligible ecobee).
facts.eligibility: New or certified refurbished, bought in Canada. Install and apply within 90 days of buying.

facts.program: Instant rebates at Manitoba retailers (Efficiency Manitoba)
facts.claim: Efficiency Manitoba's My Home page says you can save $5 or $10 instantly on select energy-efficient products at participating Manitoba retailers from September 10 to December 10.
facts.dates: September 10 to December 10 (the year is not printed on the page).
facts.notes: Status check because the year is not stated. Not shown on pages.
